frequency_question: How often do central banks deploy secondary liquidity absorption reserve ratios within a defined multi-month forward window given observable precursor conditions of systemic banking sector liquidity surplus?
membership_rule: Includes any formal announcement and implementation of an incremental, special, or secondary cash reserve ratio or supplementary reserve requirement targeted at absorbing specific liquidity surpluses by a major national central bank. Excludes standard, baseline changes to the primary statutory reserve ratio.

cases.name: PBoC reserve requirement ratio targeted/incremental adjustments
Central Bank of Malaysia special repo/reserve requirement measures
PBoC targeted RRR deployment during liquidity gluts

provenance_note: 5 cases named, 15 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (3.0x)
coverage_note: 5 named primary instances; estimated roughly 15 total comparable systemic liquidity management episodes globally where secondary reserve ratios were deployed.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller frontier market central banks where data reporting on ad-hoc reserve requirements is inconsistent.
skeleton: Global emerging market central bank liquidity management cycles involving excess liquidity neutralization tools over 30 years, grouped by distinct liquidity overhang episodes.
multiplier: 5 observed major deployments across roughly 15 comparable systemic liquidity surplus episodes globally where ad-hoc secondary reserve ratios were plausible instruments.
validity_reason: Central banking toolkits for liquidity management evolve slowly over decades, maintaining structural continuity across economic cycles.
